timeline.bobDialogue: Hi, I'm Bob Ross, and for the next 13 weeks I'll be your host. Let's go over the equipment and the eight colors we'll use every week.
We start with a big brush and cover the canvas with a thin, even coat of magic white — then long strokes back and forth so it's even all the way across.
A little bit of Cad yellow with the least touch of Phthalo green — begin making little X's, just like so.
Without cleaning the brush, we go right into some Prussian blue — making criss-cross little X strokes. Already we're beginning to have a light source.
With a nice clean brush, add just a little Titanium white in the center and work outward — blend until we have a nice blue sky.
A little Alizarin crimson and a touch of Prussian blue — just a little blue, it's a hundred times stronger. Bend the brush and push in basic tree shapes.
A little Van Dyke brown — lay in some basic trunks, and maybe a little limb right here, some little sticks and twigs.
Now we highlight these — a little white and a touch of brown mixed together. Remember where your light source is.
Now comes the fun — a little Phthalo green and a little yellow, load the brush full of paint, and push thousands of little leaves. Thin paint sticks to thick paint.
Take a little Van Dyke brown and build us a happy little path — just let it wander right down through here.
To set the path down into the painting, add some bushes that project up over the path here and there — it makes it literally drop right in.
Maybe it rained last night. Take a little touch of Prussian blue and pull downward — just pull downward, to give it a watery effect.
A little touch of Titanium white on your brush, pull down — it'll give it sort of a sheen. You can overdo this part very easily.
A little more Van Dyke brown — make little puddles out of this, and lay a brown-and-white highlight on there.
Take a little thin white paint and put some little water lines back in — literally cut right into the canvas with it. And cut a few little sticks here and there.
Put some bushes and stuff right down here on the grass — back to the Van Dyke brown and a little bit of white, then drop the bushes right in.
Let's have a happy little tree right in here. Start with the Van Dyke brown and make his little trunk — turn him out to give him little foots to stand on.
Give him some little leaves — some more Alizarin crimson and a touch of Prussian blue. We need dark in order to show light. I used a touch more Permanent red so he'll stand out.
I sign the painting with a script liner brush, a little bit of oil, and red paint. Until next week, happy painting, from all of us here.
